title: Lock inputSchema to PremiseSchema shape to prevent silent check loss
context: The published inputSchema declared premises as nested ({claim, check: {kind, path}}) but PremiseSchema is flat ({claim, path_absent | path_exists | review_by}). Zod silently strips unknown keys, so callers following the documented interface had checks discarded, producing claim-only premises that always hold — a fail-open that premise decay exists to prevent. Touches invariant(s): con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Flattened inputSchema to match PremiseSchema exactly: premises are now {claim, path_absent?, path_exists?, review_by?, attested?}. Schema lockstep is maintained with explicit comments linking to PremiseSchema in src/core/types.ts to prevent future divergence.
consequences: Premises round-trip correctly with checks preserved (no silent data loss)
Schema mismatch becomes explicit at validation time instead of masked
Agents following the documented interface now record verifiable premises
The fail-open (uncheckable premises always holding) is structurally prevented
alternatives_rejected: Keep nested schema and add runtime validation (doesn't stop the fail-open at the API boundary)
Add a nested-to-flat transformation layer (masks the schema mismatch and adds complexity)

rejected_tripwires.alternative: Keep nested schema and add runtime validation (doesn't stop the fail-open at the API boundary)
Add a nested-to-flat transformation layer (masks the schema mismatch and adds complexity)
